source.title: Steering grids for sparse-autoencoder features: when a top-context label names an activation regime rather than a causal axis

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports extensive SAE-feature steering results, but does not test feature storage under an overcomplete sparse regime, capacity competition, neuron polysemanticity, SAE feature recovery or stability, or the dimensionality of individual represented features. It discusses superposition and SAE units in related work.
record.gate_note: The reported steering outcomes concern SAE-feature effects on generated text, not whether sparse features overlap to fit more features than dimensions. Those results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version. Citations to prior work, feature-selection values, and geometric measurements used to choose matched conditions are not treated as tests of the claim.
record.test_reason: The study uses SAE decoder directions (Qwen-Scope, Gemma-Scope, Goodfire) as steering tools. It reports how single, joint and random-direction steering affect output and coherence. It never measures superposition: no toy-model storage, no capacity competition, no neuron polysemanticity, no SAE recovery of ground-truth features, no SAE stability across seeds or widths, and no test of feature dimensionality. It relies on SAE features as meaningful directions rather than merely discussing them, so T4/uses_without_test fits better than T6. The joint-necessity finding is called only 'consistent with' subspace views (Engels et al.). It is a behavioural steering result, not a test of whether a feature is one-dimensional.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also stress three points: the joint-condition effect holds at matched coefficient on all three models but only partly at matched geometry (not on Llama's suppression edge). The matched-geometry feature-vs-random result replicates on all three models. Standard loop/length detectors and NLL accept degeneration, so a diversity signal is needed.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses inference-time steering of SAE decoder directions in language models; it does not reproduce the toy-network feature-storage method.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with steering coefficient, model, feature or joint-feature condition, and coherence metric; the diagnostic steering edge differs across models.

fits_no_version.finding: Single SAE-feature steering yields distinct output regimes across coefficients: F-disc gives a contemplative voice at c=+500, Gemma #3997 a we-voice at c=-200. Joint steering of near-orthogonal selected directions damages unrelated control tasks where single-feature, unrelated-triple or geometry-matched random-direction steering does not.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested LLMs, a SAE direction's behavioural effect depends on coefficient and on co-steered directions. Top-context labels capture only one regime. Feature directions damage composition beyond magnitude-matched random directions.

fits_no_version.finding: Three individually substitutable, near-orthogonal SAE features are jointly necessary for grounded composition. The authors frame this as consistent with concepts living in subspaces, but it holds only partly at matched geometry (fails on Llama's suppression edge).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sets of SAE directions can carry a joint functional role not visible from any single direction; this bears loosely on whether SAE features are the relevant units (V5/V6-adjacent) but does not test representation dimensionality.

record.problems: The paper reports that it has no human-rated calibration of its coherence thresholds. The study covers three models; two SAEs are base-trained and applied to post-trained activations. The authors also note that the Gemma ranking pool is small and that the prevalence of mode switches is not estimated.
record.rows_left_out: Most coefficient-sweep cells, auxiliary coherence measurements, prompt-level breakdowns, and feature-triple controls are omitted because they do not test any listed claim version; the selected rows capture the main related findings. Detailed tables and appendices report the omitted steering results.

untested.parts: No toy networks, no overcomplete sparse feature storage, no sparsity-dependent transition or geometry.
No neuron-level polysemanticity and no capacity or importance allocation.
Does not measure feature spread across neurons or whether SAEs recover sparse model features. Bootstrap stability concerns the ranking of features across data pools, not SAE recovery.
Shows top-context labels miss steering regimes, but does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units. It only cites Leask et al. and Chanin et al. on that.
Joint suppression of three near-orthogonal directions is said to be consistent with subspace concepts, but no test of irreducible multi-dimensionality of a feature is run.

record.verdict_notes: Superposition (Elhage et al.) is cited only in related work. Mode-switch prevalence is explicitly not estimated; the 50-feature screen returned 0 surviving candidates. Two of three SAEs are base-trained and applied to instruct models. No verdicts are given because no row bears on any version.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test toy networks, overcomplete sparse feature storage, feature overlap, or sparsity-dependent geometric transitions.
It does not test neuron polysemanticity as a consequence of capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
It studies SAE decoder-feature steering, not polysemantic neurons or whether their polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.
It does not measure how features are distributed across neurons or test whether SAE dictionaries recover sparse model features.
It shows that top-context labels can be incomplete descriptions of steering effects, but does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units of representation.
It steers SAE decoder directions and sets of directions, but does not determine whether an individual represented feature is one-dimensional or multidimensional.

rows.subject: Qwen3-1.7B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Steered SAE feature F-disc (#26221) at c=+500 on identity-probe prompts.
rows.note: The paper reports a contemplative-philosopher voice at this coefficient, but says it is fully coherent only in a minority of samples; lexical diversity is 0.46 of baseline and 12 of 96 completions are lexically intact.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B-it
rows.operation_detail: Steered SAE feature #3997 at c=−200 on introspective prompts.

conditions.value: 3 introspective intervention prompts, 36 samples per cell

rows.note: The paper describes the we-voice as a coherent alternative surface form; lexical diversity is 0.98 of baseline and 88.9% of completions are lexically intact.

rows.subject: Qwen3-1.7B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Jointly steered F-phil, F-disc, and F-wonder at c=−500 on six intervention prompts.

conditions.value: 3 introspective and 3 control prompts, 12 samples per prompt

rows.baseline: Single F-phil at the same scalar coefficient leaves control tasks intact; rate not stated
rows.note: The paper reports placeholder-filled syntactic skeletons under joint suppression, while single-feature suppression leaves controls intact. This is a steering result about the joint role of these SAE directions, not a test of superposition.

rows.subject: Qwen3-1.7B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Steered K=50 random unit directions at c=−1000.

conditions.value: Matched to the feature-based conditions by residual-stream norm ratio and cosine

rows.baseline: Joint suppression at matched geometry: 7 of 72 (9.7%)
rows.note: The matched-geometry random-direction condition produced far fewer placeholder patterns than joint feature suppression.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B-it
rows.operation_detail: Jointly steered SAE features #3997, #13700, and #11444 at c=+200 on control prompts.
rows.note: The paper reports joint steering damage to unrelated control tasks where single-feature steering at the same coefficient leaves them intact.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Jointly steered #38565, #61417, and #23576 at c=−10 on control prompts.
rows.note: The paper reports feature-direction damage at matched geometry where the random-direction condition does not; at this suppression edge, single #38565 at matched geometry also reaches 12.5% degeneration.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
